The Hebrew uses active unnamed plural subjects for making and placing the chest; BSB uses passives.

The Hebrew repeats day in day by day; BSB says daily.

The Hebrew uses an image of healing arising for the work through their hands; BSB says the repair work progressed.

The Hebrew uses a singular subject for making the articles, where BSB presents their making as a purpose. The Hebrew uses an active plural for regularly offering burnt offerings; BSB uses the passive.
The Hebrew says he was satisfied with days; BSB uses full of years.
The Hebrew says “they buried him” and “His house”; BSB names Jehoiada, uses the passive, and says “His temple.”

Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the sender unnamed but explicitly says “to the LORD”; BSB names the LORD as sender and then uses “Him.”
The Hebrew says God’s Spirit clothed Zechariah; BSB says it came upon him.
The Hebrew says “him”; BSB names Zechariah.
The Hebrew leaves the objects of the LORD’s seeing and requiring unexpressed; BSB explicitly adds “this” and “you.”
The Hebrew says “at the turn of the year” and “the king of Damascus”; BSB says “In the spring” and “their king in Damascus.”
The Hebrew says “they executed judgments on Joash”; BSB uses the passive.
The Hebrew says “sons of Jehoiada,” in the plural; BSB says “the son of Jehoiada.” The Hebrew uses active plural subjects for burying him, where BSB uses the passive.
The Hebrew says “him”; BSB names Joash.
Close to the Hebrew.
